title: Formal Verification Write-Up POF 2828

canonical_node.axiom: The encoded ten-factor bridge matrix is internally coherent and rejects targeted semantic substitutions, conditional on the correctness of the encoded signatures.
definitions: C0 and C1: distinct coupling architectures.
C0 -> C1: one-way coupling step, irreversible relative to current transition definition.
Master Equation product: toy product that collapses to zero when any factor is zero.
LawIso: minimal binary abstraction match (value preservation, collapse preservation, bidirectional inverse mapping).
RichLawIso: adds regime-role preservation, forward transition preservation, reverse transition reflection.

BridgeMatrix: encodes ten factor slots G, M, E, S, T, K, R, Q, F, C with formal signatures, physical readings, spiritual readings, canonical bridge rows, targeted semantic swaps, and full toy product behavior.
derivation: Lean verifies C0 and C1 are distinct coupling architectures.
Lean verifies the one-way C0 -> C1 coupling step is irreversible relative to the current transition definition.
Lean verifies the toy Master Equation product collapses to zero when Q = 0.
Lean verifies Q != 0 is not sufficient for live coupling if another required factor is zero.
Lean verifies the stage sequence can reach redistribution from pre-localization and selected reverse one-step transitions are absent.
Lean verifies the named physics sequence maps to the named theology sequence by explicit order-preserving mapping.
The first LawIso model proved a two-state strong-force abstraction and a two-state love/agape abstraction match under value preservation, collapse preservation, and bidirectional inverse mapping.
Adversarial testing found a coin model with the same zero/one and collapse pattern also passed, exposing a false positive.
The richer RichLawIso layer added regime-role preservation, forward transition preservation, and reverse transition reflection.

RichLawIso accepts the enriched strong-force/love abstraction, rejects a natural coin model with random-low/random-high roles, but still accepts a deliberately relabeled coin model with constraining/liberating roles.
Lean verifies the ten canonical rows are internally consistent under the encoded signatures.

Lean rejects targeted substitutions: grace swapped with faith-commitment, entropy swapped with grace, compression swapped with communion, coherence swapped with consequence-lock, grace paired with entanglement as the physical reading.

Lean verifies full toy product behavior: every factor slot collapses the product when set to zero, R = 0 collapses the product, Q = 1 does not save the product if another required factor is zero, all ten factor slots set to 1 gives output 1.
canonical_node.action: Maintain the Lean formal verification sandbox as a working tool to verify internal coherence of encoded bridge matrices and to reject targeted semantic substitutions, while explicitly documenting that semantic grounding remains unproven.
boundary: Does not prove that encoded physical readings are complete descriptions of relevant physics.
Does not prove that encoded spiritual readings are complete descriptions of relevant theological claims.
Does not prove that every row is a strict mathematical isomorphism in the strongest sense.
Does not prove the Master Equation over real-valued fields, functions, integrals, or Mathlib-backed analysis.
Does not prove empirical claims are true.
Does not prove that external citations support each encoded signature.
Does not prove that semantic labels are independently warranted.
Does not claim that Lean has independently proved that physics and theology are structurally isomorphic in the full domain-rich sense.
test: Build cleanly with no active sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe.
Verify distinctness of C0 and C1.
Verify irreversibility of C0 -> C1 step.
Verify toy Master Equation product collapse when Q = 0.
Verify Q != 0 is not sufficient if another factor is zero.
Verify stage sequence reachability and absence of reverse one-step transitions.
Verify order-preserving mapping from physics sequence to theology sequence.
Run LawIso tests: minimal match, coin false positive detection.
Run RichLawIso tests: accept enriched abstraction, reject natural coin, accept relabeled coin (documenting semantic boundary).
Run BridgeMatrix tests: internal consistency of ten canonical rows, rejection of targeted semantic swaps, full toy product collapse behavior.

dg1_dependencies: Encoded signatures for ten-factor bridge matrix
Toy model definitions for Master Equation and stage machine
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a machine-checkable skeleton for the bridge matrix, demonstrating internal coherence and adversarial testability of encoded mappings, while explicitly bounding the claim to conditional verification.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the honest claim that the encoded bridge matrix is internally coherent and rejects several targeted semantic substitutions, conditional on signature correctness.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this node is removed, the framework loses its machine-checkable structural verification and adversarial testing capability, reducing the claim to unverified prose.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Preserve as a conditional formal verification node; do not upgrade to full domain proof.

overstatement_risks: Reading internal formal match as full external domain proof.
Claiming that Lean has independently proved structural isomorphism between physics and theology.
Treating toy model results as full physics/theology verification.
kill_conditions: If Lean specifications are found to be inconsistent with source domain semantics.
If semantic labels are shown to be unfaithful to the source domains.
If the encoded signatures are found to be incomplete or incorrect.
risk.lean_target: Encode richer invariants for each factor (M, S, R, Q, G, E, K, F, T, C) and add semantic-swap, same-domain wrong-mechanism, same-mechanism wrong-direction, and false-positive clone tests.

plain_summary: This document reports the current state of Lean formal verification for the ten-factor bridge matrix. It shows that the encoded matrix is internally coherent and rejects several targeted semantic substitutions, but it explicitly states that this is conditional on the correctness of the encoded signatures and does not constitute a full domain proof. The document is honest about the boundaries and recommends further work to make signatures harder to fake.
